Tear-off widgets

Three ordinary widgets. Pull one out of the page, into a new window, an always-on-top window, another tab, or another origin, and it keeps working: what you do out there is sent back and happens to the real element here. Drag a grip ⠿ outside this window, onto the dock tab, or pick a route from the menu.

The routes

There are only two ways for a piece of a page to appear in another window, and this page does both.

  • Move the real element. A window you opened is a same-origin document you can reach, so popup.document.body.append(element) adopts the live node. Its listeners, timers and state come with it, because they belong to this page's script. It is real DOM out there: selectable, accessible, native input. It only works while a window reference exists, on the same origin.
  • Stream it and replay input. The element never leaves. HTML-in-canvas gives its pixels on every paint; they travel as ImageBitmaps, video or JPEGs and input comes back as small messages. This works over anything that carries a message, including routes with no window reference at all.
Show the code tearing a widget off

Each widget is ordinary markup inside a <live-region>. w.surface is that region's surface, w.content the widget's root element and win the window just opened.

  1. Load the pieces.
  2. Stream to a popup (same or another origin): post it a MessagePort and serve the surface on the other end.
  3. The window it opens. A <live-view> and a few ways to get connected. It holds no DOM from this page.
  4. Or move the real element. append() into the other window's document adopts the node. No canvas involved.
  5. Or float it as a video. The surface is a MediaStream, so classic Picture-in-Picture works.
  6. Or share it with a tab that has no link to this one, through a relay room and then WebRTC.
  7. Inside <live-region>: a shadow root with a drawable canvas and a slot. Your markup is slotted into the canvas, so it can be drawn without being moved.
  8. Inside: on every paint event, draw the element.
  9. Inside: copy the pixels to a second canvas, and black out private fields. That second canvas is the only thing that ever leaves the page.
  10. Inside: hand the copy out as an ImageBitmap or a MediaStream.
  11. Inside: replay the input that comes back on the real elements.
  12. The whole library.

ResultExperimentDetail

One experiment is not run automatically because it can take the tab down:

Findings

  • Interaction does get back to the origin without any window link. A noopener tab reaches the source over BroadcastChannel (ImageBitmaps clone across it), through a SharedWorker that hands both tabs one end of a MessageChannel, or through the Worker's relay room. Even localStorage events work as a transport.
  • Across origins with no link, you need a meeting point. The relay room works anywhere. A frame from the source's origin embedded in the other page can also bridge to BroadcastChannel. Browsers that partition third-party storage are expected to cut that bridge when the two pages are different sites; headless Chromium 157 did not, so check the row above in your own browser.
  • A scripted about:blank popup needs no messaging at all. The opener calls into the popup's document directly and hands it ImageBitmaps by reference.
  • The source page has to be on screen for streaming. paint stops when the tab is hidden, so a streamed widget freezes while you are in another tab. Moving the real DOM into a Picture-in-Picture window does not have that problem, because the element is then painted by that window.
  • Video Picture-in-Picture is view only, but not button-less. Media Session actions show as buttons on the video window, and this page maps them to the widget's own buttons.
